derivation:
1755. Explicit source-compatible full Haar coordinates and marked-kernel pullback on a declared gauge chart. This is an intermediate raw-kernel calculation, NOT a Jacobian of the final axial-to-Landau section.

Fix the original finite periodic fine lattice, compact group G, real/unitary reference field U0, original physical domain D, pointwise original density F, exterior coordinates E_fix and their data V0, and the already chosen physical mean M_fix. No coupling, cutoff, original gauge factor, mean or domain is changed. The RG torus must admit a compatible native anchored L-block partition, used ONLY as auxiliary coordinates on the SAME fine field lattice. Its roots R need not be identified with physical coarse endpoints. Every physical endpoint below is its ACTUAL fine site. A lack of such an auxiliary compatible partition in the actual instance is a gate; no new torus is substituted.

Choose in every native block a rooted spanning tree whose root-to-site paths are the source canonical coordinate paths Gamma_rz. Those paths form a comb tree with n-1 edges for n sites, without periodic edges inside a block. Let T be the disjoint union of those trees. One independent oriented representative per original fine link is used; reversing a tree edge uses Haar-invariant group inversion. Put P_rz=U0(Gamma_rz). Define the group-field axial coordinate space S0 by Y(Gamma_rz)=P_rz, equivalently Y_e=U0_e on the tree edges. Its coordinates are the ORIGINAL non-tree link values, with product normalized Haar measure dY_free.

Let K be the ordinary point-fixed gauge group: k(r)=I at native roots, independent normalized Haar variables k(z) at every other fine site. Let C be an open admissible chart in K on which all source logarithms below are defined on the SAME chosen branch. For k in C define the actual source gauge average (78), since k(r)=I,

 a_r(k)=exp[ sum_{z in B(r)} L^(-d) Log(Ad_{P_rz} k(z)) ],
 g_r(k)=a_r(k)^(-1),
 l_g(z)=P_rz^(-1) g_r P_rz,  z in B(r),
 u(k)(z)=l_g(z) k(z).

These are group-valued quantities, not Lie-algebra approximations. The full gauge average A0(q)(r) of (78) is q(r) exp[sum L^(-d) Log(q(r)^(-1) Ad_{P_rz}q(z))]. Hence A0(l_g k)(r)=g_r a_r(k), exactly, and A0(u(k))=I. The averaged-zero set is NOT called a group. Its parametrization by k is one-to-one on the chart: given q with A0(q)=I, set g_r=q(r), k=l_g^(-1)q, then k(r)=I and g_r=a_r(k)^(-1). Conjugations and all multiplication orders must be retained.

Define the full coordinate map

       Psi(Y,k)=Y^(u(k)^(-1)),
       Psi_b=u(b_minus)^(-1) Y_b u(b_plus).

It is not the dimension-reducing map U -> Y alone. The pair (Y,k) has the original number of field coordinates: (#links-#sites+#roots)+(#sites-#roots)=#links. Its inverse can be constructed without an unknown implicit solver. For a full original field U let k_U(z)=P_rz^(-1) U(Gamma_rz), k_U(r)=I; then Z=U^(k_U) lies in S0. Compute g=a(k_U)^(-1), and set Y=Z^(l_g). Because P_child=P_parent U0_e on a tree, l_g preserves every fixed tree value U0_e; thus Y also lies in S0. With gauge composition (V^a)^b=V^(b a),

       Y^(u^-1)=(Z^(l_g))^(k_U^-1 l_g^-1)=Z^(k_U^-1)=U.

Conversely the point-rooted tree gauge of Psi(Y,k) is exactly k. The chart image is precisely the fields with k_U in C; call it U_C. Thus Psi is a genuine full-coordinate local diffeomorphism S0 x C -> U_C. It imposes no Landau condition on Y and does not identify the native source Sigma image with the physical fiber.

THE HAAR JACOBIAN IS COMPUTED, not named as a new premise. First use the ordinary tree coordinates U=Z^(k^-1). On every rooted tree, from root outward, U_e=k(parent)^(-1) U0_e k(child). At a fixed parent, normalized Haar in U_e is normalized Haar in k(child). This is a triangular change over the trees. Every non-tree U_b=k(b_minus)^(-1) Z_b k(b_plus) is a left/right translation of its independent Z_b at fixed k. Therefore dU=dZ_free dk exactly. At fixed k, the further Z -> Y=Z^(l_g(k)) preserves the tree constraints and left/right translates each free link. Its free-link Haar Jacobian is1. Dependence of l_g on k gives off-diagonal blocks in the full change (Z,k)->(Y,k), but its k coordinate is unchanged; the triangular full determinant remains1. Hence

                         dU=dY_free dk       on U_C.

No extra coarse-root gauge volume is divided out or integrated twice; coarse-frame degrees remain among Y's free links. No Haar measure on a non-group is invented. Separately, the delta-weighted SITE gauge measure gives the same k measure: write any q=l_g k with g_r=q(r), k(r)=I. Product site Haar is dg dk by the same triangular left-translation argument. On k in C, A0(q)=g a(k), so integrating the normalized group deltas delta_G(g_r a_r(k)) over dg gives exactly1 and leaves dk. Chart restrictions stay in this formula; it does not assign unit total mass to C or to an arbitrary final gauge slice. This is a full-coordinate/delta-weighted averaged-gauge Jacobian, NOT a unit Faddeev-Popov determinant for a final Landau restriction.

Now carry the UNCHANGED physical constraints through Psi. For coarse data V on its actual original row set, define
 V^u(c)=u(c_minus) V(c) u(c_plus)^(-1).
 For the original prescribed fine exterior set define
 V0^u(b)=u(b_minus) V0(b) u(b_plus)^(-1), b in E_fix.
 Both use actual endpoint sites, not a guessed identification of physical endpoints with native roots. Physical point-gauge equivariance gives M_fix(Psi(Y,k))(c)=u(c_minus)^(-1) M_fix(Y)(c) u(c_plus), for either already chosen CMP109(0.4) or(0.12) on its admitted domain. Conjugation invariance of the normalized group delta gives

 delta_G(M_fix(Psi) V^-1)=delta_G(M_fix(Y) (V^u)^(-1)),
 delta_G(Psi_b V0_b^-1)=delta_G(Y_b (V0^u_b)^(-1)).

These targets depend on k; they must not be frozen to their original numerical values. At native roots u(r)=g_r, but that simplification is used only when an actual physical endpoint coincides with that root. In particular u(k) may be nonidentity outside X even if the point-gauge coordinate k was supported inside X. All original fine exterior constraints remain, with these transported targets; this is NOT a claim that Psi preserves the fixed-exterior fiber pointwise.

Operational chart-part identity, with every original constraint included ONCE:

 K_C(V,V0;J)=int_{k in C} dk int_{S0} dY_free 1_D(Psi(Y,k)) F(Psi(Y,k);V,V0,J)
       * product_original_coarse_rows delta_G(M_fix(Y)(c) (V^u(c))^-1)
       * product_original_fixed_fine_links delta_G(Y_b (V0^u(b))^-1).

The original chart part on the left uses full fine Haar and the same coarse constraints/fixed-exterior Dirac embedding, restricted only by k_U in C. This formula is rigorously a joint weak pushforward identity in (V,V0) for the original actual graph density. If F depends on the data, require integrability of its actual graph evaluation F(U;M_fix(U),U_Efix,J); arbitrary ambient L1 equivalence classes do not supply fiber traces. At a fixed target it applies only to an already admitted original constrained measure with its needed integrability/branch meaning. The coordinate map does not by itself prove existence of that conditional measure. Redundant outside coarse constraints, if present in the original kernel, remain the same original factors; none is squared, silently solved or replaced by an independent normalizer.

The physical domain D is NOT replaced by a box in Y or k. Its full pullback is retained. Nor is the logarithm chart asserted to cover D: the original kernel is K=K_C+K_out, where K_out is the original unchanged integral on k_U outside C. No outside-chart weight is discarded, even if a future estimate might make it small. A partition/cover and uniform physical parameter chain remain needed to treat the whole domain by such charts. An original additional singular gauge constraint, if present, needs its admitted measure interpretation and full pullback; no independent product-of-distributions theorem is supplied here. For the original exponential gauge density, all its actual factors are ordinary factors within F.

MARKS AND ACTION. For real unitary integration and compact gauge u, the original Wilson action is gauge invariant: A(Psi(Y,k))=A(Y). Every noninvariant cutoff, gauge density, sector function and normalization stays pulled back as part of F; unchanged action does not justify discarding them. A complete closed rooted word with root r transforms as Phi_r(Psi)=u(r)^(-1) Phi_r(Y) u(r), with every root transport included. A matrix source in tr(J_r Phi_r) is therefore transported to u(r) J_r u(r)^(-1). Complex J is allowed coefficientwise in a finite polynomial source algebra, under the original integrability assumptions; no positivity of a complex density is used.

Classify a mark by the support of its WHOLE rooted word. An interior word remains the full transformed word. A crossing word is never split into independent inside and outside factors. If the entire original word uses E_fix, its original value on the fixed-data constraint is Phi_r(V0) and it factors ONCE with its original matrix order. On the pulled-back constraint its Y word is Phi_r(V0^u)=u(r)Phi_r(V0)u(r)^(-1); the surrounding u(r)^(-1) and u(r) restore the same original value. It is incorrect to factor Phi_r(Y) itself as a constant without those constraints and root frames. A traced closed mark is invariant. An open endpoint word uses the corresponding two endpoint factors rather than an invented single-root conjugation.

Any normalized identity must use the same FULL original denominator, including K_out and every original outer factor, whenever that denominator is already known nonzero. This calculation does not prove positivity/nonvanishing, connected-log expansions, infinite sector/history exchanges, a uniform source profile, original P1 repair, Landau-section Jacobians, H/Hsharp identification, or a physical manuscript result. It computes one explicit raw-gauge coordinate Jacobian and the corresponding complete chart-part constraint/mark pullback. Falsifiers include an error in gauge composition, tree inverse, Haar triangularity, native average parametrization, moving target orientation, or root-source conjugation. Preserve any such failure rather than substituting a different mean, exterior, field domain, cutoff or an unspecified determinant.
